source_span: Of this increase, >$100B was for supply and capacity for F2028/C2027 - signaling strong conviction in revenue growth in C2027 and backing its guidance raise, while supply for F2029/C2028 did not go up much at all
source_chain: A: NVDA added >$100B to C2027 supply commitments (total supply $311B to $430B), confirming conviction in 2027 revenue and backing the guidance raise, easing 2027-cut fears. Therefore B: C2028 commitments barely moved (unlike last quarter's large step-up), so UBS's worry shifts from a 2027 cut to how hard growth decelerates in 2028. Therefore C: UBS trims 2028 growth to <10% Y/Y (EPS ~$18.80) and cuts PT to $220 from $240, keeping Buy. Invalidation: a big increase in 2028 commitments next quarter would have mollified the deceleration fear; continued flatness supports it.
pulse_chain: A: '>$100 billion of the increase in purchase commitments was for 2027 capacity, which UBS reads as conviction in 2027 demand.' Therefore B: 'Commitments for 2028 barely moved... That is why UBS's worry has moved from a 2027 cut to how hard growth decelerates in 2028.' Therefore C: 'it trimmed its 2028 growth estimate to just under 10% with earnings of about $18.80 a share, cutting its price target to $220 from $240 while keeping its Buy rating.' Invalidation: 'If the 2028 commitment line is flat again, UBS has the right read.'
why: The pulse keeps UBS's full chain in order and direction (2027 commits up eases 2027 fear, 2028 commits flat shifts the worry to 2028 deceleration, hence the trim/PT cut/kept Buy) and preserves the same flat-vs-up invalidation on 2028 commitments, with only the delayed-10-Q detail loosely stitched onto it as compression rather than a reversed or swapped condition.
